Order: roster and the cap (TEAM-CV-001 to 003), then Aeldari Raiders and Veteran Raider (TEAM-CV-004 to 006, they shape every activation), Rifles (TEAM-CV-007), then the operatives.
- Team-local weapon rules the scaffold leaves out: `cv.a.wr-psychic` (freezing grasp, lightning strike, witch staff). The Felarch's weapons (neuro disruptor, shuriken rifle, shuriken pistol, power weapon) carry none.
- RULING lines expected: blaster and wraithcannon, weapons without Range, low crit Dmg, Faolchú's Bond errata (Confirmed), Veteran Raider, One Step Ahead trigger and APL penalty, Blademaster distance, Bladed Stance use, Faolchú's Bond use, Erudite Hunter, Blink Pack distance, Slicing Attack line, Soul Heal self-target, Quick on the Trigger targets, on guard (Confirmed, FAQ) and replacing point-blank, Pistol Barrage, Prowling Raiders, Warp Fold picks and restriction, Warding Shield, lasting PSYCHIC effects and Null Rod, Rifles outside its activation, Aeldari Raiders as a cost change, Plunderers, Mobile Engagement moved, Outcasts, Opportunistic Fighters, Light Fingers in v1, Capricious Flight and Veteran Raider, Contemptuous Adventurer, Diuturnal Mantles, Mistfield, Runes of Guidance, Star Charts.
- Gotchas: section 14.10. The free Dash is a cost change inside the operative's own activation only (never in counteractions); the Felarch's free action replaces it. Quick on the Trigger needs the point-blank transport for free Shoots and Guard until the shared fix lands. Nine operatives use the 9-operative kill grade row.

### 14.13 As built (M10)

Built as mapped in 14.11, `playable: true`; tests are `TEAM-CV-000` to `TEAM-CV-035` in `tests/engine/teams/corsair-voidscarred.test.ts` (scenarios for the 28 code hooks in `corsair-voidscarred.hooks.ts`). Differences from the plan:

- The data names 28 code hooks. Passive rules (Rifles, Aeldari Raiders, Veteran Raider, Camo Cloak, Bladed Stance, Faolchú's Bond, Blink Pack, Quick on the Trigger, Prowling Raiders, Diuturnal Mantles, Mistfield, Runes of Guidance) only register a name and `markFired` where the rule applies; the three strategy flag ploys share `cvFlagPloy`.
- Plunderers raises its picks one at a time through an `ability.choice` (with a "done" option), like Divert and Disappear, and then calls `resumeGambit`; the ban lands only on an operative whose free Dash finished.
- One Step Ahead's free Shoot is offered only when the Felarch can Shoot (a Conceal order bars it). Mistfield is offered only when the weapon has Piercing. Both are RULING lines.
- Tokens exist for One Step Ahead and Faolchú's Bond (added at the turning point start while unspent), Runes of Guidance (while the turning point use is unspent), Warding Shield (the shield itself: it goes with the Way Seeker's next activation or incapacitation) and Erudite Hunter. Mistfield has no token.
- Slicing Attack records the warp jump in the `afterMove` of its code hook (the Reposition's move event carries a `fly` segment) and offers the cut as a 0 CP pseudo ploy in `firefight.actionEnded`. The line does not pass through obstructing terrain: `slicingReach` bends it round a part's corners or takes it over the part, and that route must be 7" or less.
- No shared-engine change was needed; the fallbacks of 14.9 (Blademaster action, point-blank transport, `moveSurcharge` veto, Slicing Attack line geometry, Warp Fold swap) are as written.

## 15. Warpcoven

Rule IDs `T-WC.<n>`, checklist IDs `TEAM-WC-<nnn>`. Sources: the Warpcoven team PDF (Kill Team 2024, Faction version 3, April '26 update log state; the layout and flow extracts were read together, and the update log's errata and rules commentary are applied) as the primary source, cross-checked against the Wahapedia Warpcoven page (Faction version 3; its header still says January '26, but its text already carries the April '26 items: Rubric Marine Save 2+, the Astral Bombardment and Master of the Immaterium additions, the new Brotherhood of Sorcerers, Aetherial Warding and Psychic Cabal wording, and the Psychic Cabal FAQ). The two agree on every stat and weapon; they differ in four places of wording, listed in 15.10, where the PDF update log wins. Facts read from the PDF are Confirmed; our own calls are Unsourced. All rule text is restated in our own words; team, operative, weapon, ploy, boon and equipment names are used as printed. Core terms per `10-rules-core.md` (R-x.y), missions and universal equipment per `11-missions.md` (M-x.y). Ploys and equipment are one bullet per record so each can carry its MECH line.

Weapon type column: R = ranged, M = melee. Dmg is `normal/crit`. Base is in mm.

### 15.1 Team selection

- T-WC.1 Roster is exactly 5 selections from one list (T-WC.2). There is no leader slot and no LEADER keyword in this edition of the team (the update log deleted the old "one SORCERER is the LEADER, +1 wound" clause). Each TZAANGOR operative counts as half a selection, so a roster fields 5 to 9 operatives.
  - MECH: team.json one slot `main`, `count: 5`, `halfSelections` = the four Tzaangor datacards; no leader slot | CLASS: data
  - RULING: Warpcoven no leader | the team has no LEADER operative; the scaffold's first datacard (Sorcerer of Destiny) is not a leader, and any rule of another team that names "the LEADER" finds none on this team | the April '26 update log deletes the LEADER clause and no Warpcoven datacard prints the keyword | Confirmed
  - RULING: Warpcoven odd Tzaangor | an odd number of Tzaangors rounds up (a lone Tzaangor uses a whole selection), so the slot still needs exactly 5 selections | "two halves make one selection" leaves an unpaired half unused, and the roster validator's `slotCost` already rounds halves up | Unsourced
- T-WC.2 List: SORCERER OF DESTINY, SORCERER OF TEMPYRION, SORCERER OF WARPFIRE, RUBRIC MARINE GUNNER, RUBRIC MARINE ICON BEARER, RUBRIC MARINE WARRIOR, TZAANGOR CHAMPION, TZAANGOR HORN BEARER, TZAANGOR ICON BEARER, TZAANGOR WARRIOR. At least one SORCERER must be taken. Every WARRIOR (Rubric Marine Warrior and Tzaangor Warrior) may be taken any number of times; every other entry at most once (so at most three Sorcerers, one of each, and one Gunner).
  - MECH: slot `repeatable: ["wc.rubric-marine-warrior", "wc.tzaangor-warrior"]`; team `selection.caps: [{ keyword: "SORCERER", min: 1 }]` | CLASS: data
  - RULING: Warpcoven repeatable entries | both WARRIOR cards are repeatable, the Gunner is not | "other than WARRIOR operatives" names a keyword both Warrior cards carry, and the update log deleted the old GUNNER exception | Confirmed
- T-WC.3 Loadouts:
  - Each SORCERER: force stave and the PSYCHIC ranged weapons printed on its card (Destiny: doombolt; Tempyrion: fluxblast; Warpfire: firestorm and mindburn), plus one of inferno bolt pistol, Prosperine khopesh or warpflame pistol.
  - RUBRIC MARINE GUNNER: warpflamer and fists, or soulreaper cannon (both profiles) and fists.
  - RUBRIC MARINE ICON BEARER, RUBRIC MARINE WARRIOR: inferno boltgun and fists (fixed).

- T-WC.4 Archetypes: RECON, SECURITY (tac ops out of scope for v1).

- T-WC.5 Keywords: every operative is WARPCOVEN and CHAOS. Sorcerers add HERETIC ASTARTES, PSYKER, SORCERER and DESTINY, TEMPYRION or WARPFIRE; Rubric Marines add HERETIC ASTARTES, RUBRIC MARINE and their role (GUNNER, ICON BEARER, WARRIOR); Tzaangors add TZAANGOR and their role (CHAMPION, HORN BEARER, ICON BEARER, WARRIOR). Tzaangors are not HERETIC ASTARTES, so ASTARTES (T-WC.31) never covers them. The chosen BOON OF TZEENTCH is not a keyword (T-WC.21).

Another team's Null Rod (Novitiate Condemnor) switches these off within 6" of the Condemnor, and the Condemnor cannot be picked by them. There is no perils, no psychic test and no Manifest action in this edition.
  - MECH: weapons carry `wc.a.wr-psychic`; the five abilities have `keywords: ["PSYCHIC"]`; shared files already block PSYCHIC actions and PSYCHIC ranged weapons (`psychicAllowed`); team code asks `psychicSelectable` before a PSYCHIC action picks an operative and `psychicAllowed` before every lasting PSYCHIC effect applies (T-WC.7 to T-WC.12) | CLASS: generic:psychic
  - RULING: Warpcoven PSYCHIC lasting effects under Null Rod | Protected by Fate, Ravage Destiny, Alight, Mindburn tokens and Temporal Flux have no effect at a moment when an operative they touch (the beneficiary, the affected enemy, or the shooter) is within a Condemnor's Null Rod distance; the token stays and works again once out of range | the Novitiates commentary says an operative cannot benefit from, be selected for or use a PSYCHIC rule while in range, and that PSYCHIC rules have no effect within that distance | Confirmed

### 15.4 Operative rules and unique actions

- T-WC.7 **PROTECTED BY FATE** (Sorcerer of Destiny, 1 AP, PSYCHIC): pick one friendly WARPCOVEN operative visible to the Sorcerer (itself included). Until the Sorcerer's next activation starts, the Sorcerer is incapacitated, or any friendly operative performs this action again (whichever is first), whenever that operative is being shot its player may re-roll any of its defence dice. Not while in an enemy's control range.
  - MECH: unique action with a friendly-target choice (visible); token `wc.protected` (cap 1, one live token per seat: a new use removes the old one), expiries `sourceActivationStart` and `sourceIncapacitated`; `modifyDefenceDice` adds `RerollGrant { mode: 'any' }` when the target holds the token and `psychicAllowed` holds for it | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Warpcoven "until it's incapacitated" | in Protected by Fate, Ravage Destiny and Alight the "it" is the Sorcerer that performed the action: its incapacitation ends the effect; the picked operative's own removal ends it anyway | the clause would add nothing if it meant the picked operative, and it sits in the list of the performer's timers | Unsourced
  - RULING: Warpcoven Protected by Fate self-target | the Sorcerer may pick itself | an operative is visible to and within any distance of itself (R-8.3) and the text does not say "other" | Confirmed
- T-WC.8 **RAVAGE DESTINY** (Sorcerer of Destiny, 1 AP, PSYCHIC): pick one enemy operative visible to and within 9" of the Sorcerer (12" with Master of the Immaterium). With the same three end conditions as T-WC.7: (a) whenever that enemy is shooting, fighting or retaliating, its player must re-roll every attack die showing 6; (b) when marker control is worked out, that enemy's APL counts as 1 lower (not an APL change, so it stacks with APL changes and ignores R-9.6). Not while in an enemy's control range.
  - MECH: unique action with an enemy-target choice (visible, within the distance, `psychicSelectable`); token `wc.ravaged` (as T-WC.7); attack hook `diceRolled` calls `attack-common.forcedReroll` on the holder's attack dice showing 6 (shooting, and both fight roles); provider `controlApl` returns apl - 1 for the holder | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Warpcoven Ravage Destiny forced re-roll | applied at once after the holder's attack roll, before any optional re-roll; the forced dice cannot be re-rolled again; defence dice and cover saves are untouched | a die can be re-rolled only once (R-9.2) and the rule names attack dice; same as the Omen ruling (T-HA.23) | Unsourced
- T-WC.9 **RECONSTITUTION RITUAL** (Sorcerer of Tempyrion, 1 AP, PSYCHIC): one friendly WARPCOVEN operative visible to and within 6" (9" with Master of the Immaterium) regains up to 2D3 lost wounds. Not while in an enemy's control range, and not if any friendly operative already performed this action this TP.
  - MECH: unique action with a friendly-target filter (visible, within the distance); `effects.regainWounds(2D3)`; team-wide once-per-TP ledger (counts a use borrowed through Psychic Cabal) | CLASS: data (limit part team-hook)
  - RULING: Warpcoven Reconstitution Ritual self-target | the Tempyrion may heal itself | an operative is within any distance of itself (R-8.3) | Confirmed
- T-WC.10 **TEMPORAL FLUX** (Sorcerer of Tempyrion, 1 AP, PSYCHIC): pick one friendly WARPCOVEN operative visible to and within 6" (9" with Master of the Immaterium) and place your Temporal Flux marker within that operative's control range. At the end of that operative's next activation: if it is not incapacitated and is wholly within 6" of the marker (never extended), remove it and set it up again in a placeable spot with the marker in its control range (or as near as possible), then remove the marker; otherwise just remove the marker. Not while in an enemy's control range or while your Temporal Flux marker is in the killzone.
  - MECH: unique action placing a team marker in the target's control range (`placementSpots`); `activation.end` handler for the marked operative: set `pos` to the placeable spot nearest the marker, emit `OperativeMoved` with action `'forced'` and one `'fly'` segment (the brief's re-place fallback), remove the marker; `operative.incapacitated` removes the marker | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Warpcoven Temporal Flux "next activation" | the activation in which the action was performed never counts (picking itself, the Tempyrion returns at the end of its following activation); a counteraction is not an activation, so it neither triggers nor uses up the effect | "next activation" is the core term and counteracting is instead of activating | Confirmed
  - RULING: Warpcoven Temporal Flux set-up spot | team code sets the operative up at the placeable spot nearest the marker (the marker inside its control range when possible), keeping its order and facing; it may end within an enemy's control range; no decision is raised | lifecycle hooks never raise decisions, the rule names no other limit, and the nearest spot is the one the text asks for | Unsourced
  - RULING: Warpcoven Temporal Flux under Null Rod | no set-up if the operative was activated within, or ends its activation within, a Condemnor's Null Rod distance; the marker is then removed | the Warpcoven rules commentary answers "no to both"; removing the marker follows the rule's own "otherwise" branch | Confirmed
  - RULING: Warpcoven Temporal Flux after incapacitation | the marker is removed as soon as the picked operative is incapacitated | the rule removes the marker whenever the operative is not wholly within 6", incapacitation included, and an incapacitated operative has no next activation | Unsourced

Neither source prints a cost: every ploy is 1 CP (R-2.4). Strategy ploys last until the end of the TP (R-2.5). Each firefight ploy at most once per TP.

In this TP's Firefight phase, in any shooting, fighting or retaliating sequence (either player's), after attack dice are rolled and before re-rolls, you may replace one D6 rolled for that sequence (yours or the opponent's) with one reserved die. The replacement keeps that value: it cannot be changed or re-rolled, and if it is not a success (or not a crit) it cannot be retained as one; it is discarded when the sequence ends. ### 15.9 Generic capabilities (survey; resolved in the Engine map below)

- **operativeChoices** (built, batch C): the boon pick per Sorcerer (`forKeyword`, `unique`, `keyword: false`), changeable by `setOperativePick`. Used by T-WC.21, T-WC.29, T-WC.43.
- **halfSelections and selection.caps min** (built): five selections, Tzaangors half, at least one SORCERER. Used by T-WC.1, T-WC.2. **loadoutCaps** (built): one warpflame pistol, one soulreaper cannon. Used by T-WC.3.
- **psychic** (built, batch C): PSYCHIC tag and action keyword, `psychicAllowed`, `psychicSelectable`. Used by T-WC.6 to T-WC.12.
- **forcedReroll + controlApl** (built): Ravage Destiny. **applyAplEffect** at `activation.start`: Sorcerous Automata. **canFly**: Immaterial Flight. **blockCapacity**: Shield. **joinActivation**: Mutant Herd. **markerActionRelief**: Mutant Appendage. **reactions** + `startFreeAction`: Savage Brutality. **weaponForbidden**: Psychic Cabal and ASTARTES.
- Team-local fallbacks named in the brief: borrowed weapons (Psychic Cabal), reserved dice (Fate Itself), re-placing without a path (Temporal Flux), counteraction extra action (Echoes from the Warp).
- **Gaps found here (not in the brief's tables)**:
  - `repeatSurchargeGroup` (NICE): `abilities.repeatSurcharge` compares profile ids, so a soulreaper cannon Shoot with the other profile escapes the +1 AP. Resolved in the batch C prep: `repeatSurcharge` now treats two profiles of one profile group as the same weapon (GEN-085), so the `astartes` code param covers the soulreaper cannon's focused / sweeping switch with no team code.
  - `dieLock` (NICE): no flag stops other rules (Rending, Severe, Punishing, another team's conversions) from reclassifying a Fate Itself replacement die. Fallback: tag the die `wc.fate` and re-derive its kind from its value in the team's own `afterAttackRoll` handler; a conversion made later by another team's hook may still slip through (RULING Fate Itself errata applies as far as the hooks allow).
  - `conditionalPick` (NICE): Astral Bombardment needs a weapon pick only for the Warpfire and only with that boon. Fallback: an unconditional `bombard` operative choice on WARPFIRE (`keyword: false`) read only while the boon is Astral Bombardment; the Team Builder shows it for every Warpfire.
  - `activationEndDecision` (NICE): Temporal Flux's set-up spot is a player choice at activation end, where hooks cannot ask. Fallback: nearest placeable spot (RULING).
  - `perDieDefenderPloy` (NICE): All Is Dust is a per-die choice. Fallback: pre-commit in `shoot.defenceRolled` / `fight.rolled` (RULING).

### 15.10 Gotchas

- PDF update log over Wahapedia in two places with practical effect, each with a Corrected ruling: Fate Itself's replacement die cannot be changed or turned into a crit; Capricious Plan gives Dash and/or order change. Two more are wording only: Wahapedia's ASTARTES says "friendly HERETIC ASTARTES" without WARPCOVEN, and its Brotherhood of Sorcerers omits "instead" (same meaning). The Sorcerous Scrolls precedence sentence and the Arcane Robes per-Sorcerer sentence exist only in the update log.
- No LEADER, no leader slot: 5 selections, Tzaangors are halves, at least one Sorcerer. A roster fields 5 to 9 operatives, so the kill grade row follows the actual starting count. Both WARRIOR cards repeat; the Gunner does not.
- ASTARTES here has no bolt-weapon condition (unlike T-AOD.15, T-PM.16, T-LG.27): a Gunner may Shoot twice with its warpflamer or soulreaper cannon for +1 AP on the second (across both soulreaper profiles). The same PSYCHIC ranged weapon never twice in one activation (doombolt then inferno bolt pistol is fine; firestorm then mindburn is fine). Tzaangors are not HERETIC ASTARTES: one Shoot, one Fight, Engage order to counteract.
- Sorcerous Automata makes a Rubric APL 2 when no Sorcerer is within 9" at activation start: then its two Shoots with a heavy weapon (1 + 2 AP) are impossible. It never affects counteractions.
- Boons are tags on Sorcerers only, unique across the roster, public. Sorcerous Scrolls changes one once per battle, also at a counteraction.
- Astral Bombardment on the doombolt replaces Devastating 2 with 2" Devastating 2 (hits friends within 2" of the target too); on firestorm or mindburn it is Seek Light or Devastating 1 per Shoot, never both, so Devastating 1 costs the printed Seek Light.
- Master of the Immaterium extends Ravage Destiny, Reconstitution Ritual and Temporal Flux's pick, never Temporal Flux's 6" return check, Psychic Cabal's 9" or any non-PSYCHIC distance.
- Mindburn: only crit damage dealt in the Resolve step gives the token; Hit worse by 1 on every weapon of the holder, not with injury; it ends when the holder's next activation ends or when any friendly operative uses mindburn again.
- Ravage Destiny forces re-rolls of 6s (crits included) on the enemy's attack dice and lowers its control APL by 1 (not an APL change). Protected by Fate gives the friendly defender any re-rolls. Both, and Alight, end at the performing Sorcerer's next activation start, its incapacitation, or a new use of the same action by any friendly operative.
- Temporal Flux: one marker at a time; return at the end of the target's next activation (never a counteraction), only if wholly within 6" of the marker and not under Null Rod; the set-up may land in an enemy's control range.
- Null Rod (another team) shuts off these PSYCHIC actions, the four PSYCHIC ranged weapons and every lasting PSYCHIC effect within 6" of the Condemnor; the force stave loses its weapon rules there (the Novitiates' side applies that), so Brotherhood of Sorcerers adds nothing to it.
- Savage Brutality: one extra free Fight per activation of the Champion, after its first Fight, against any enemy. Brayhorn is 0 AP (not a counteraction) and lasts to the next Ready step. Herd Banner cuts Normal Dmg 3+ by 1 on Tzaangors within 3" of the Icon Bearer. Shield is Save 4+ always, and double blocks only while fighting with that weapon.
- Slow and Purposeful: Ceaseless unless the Warrior Charged or Repositioned earlier in the activation; Dash and Fall Back keep it; always on in a counteraction.
- Fate Itself: attack dice only, one reserved die per sequence, the second die survives only if the pair summed to 9 or more; leftovers vanish at TP end.
- Edition leaks to reject: no 2021 Warpcoven (no psychic phase or Manifest Psychic Power action, no perils of the warp, no Cabbalistic rituals or psychic powers table, no 2021 All Is Dust "+1 save"), no 40k 10th Thousand Sons (no Cabal of Sorcerers points, no Rituals, no 4++ invulnerable save; the only 4+ is the Shield Save); inches only, three defence dice, every printed number from the April '26 cards.

### 15.13 As built (M10 batch C)

Files: `src/data/teams/warpcoven/*.json`, `src/engine/teams/warpcoven.ts`, `src/client/teams/warpcoven.ts`, `tests/engine/teams/warpcoven.{test,hooks}.ts` (15 tests, TEAM-WC-000 to TEAM-WC-034; 24 hook scenarios). Ids: `wc.sorcerer-of-destiny`, `wc.sorcerer-of-tempyrion`, `wc.sorcerer-of-warpfire`, `wc.rubric-marine-{gunner,icon-bearer,warrior}`, `wc.tzaangor-{champion,horn-bearer,icon-bearer,warrior}`; boon ability records `wc.a.boon-*` (text only; one hook `boonsOfTzeentch`). Differences from the brief, each with a RULING in `needs-rules-check.md`:
- The SORCERER minimum is a `selection.caps` entry by datacard ids (`from`, `min: 1`) instead of by keyword, because the shared adapter test validates default rosters without the datacards.
- Savage Brutality is a 0 CP offer in the active player's `firefight.actionEnded` window (the `reactions` provider is only asked of the non-active seat). The free Fight starts through `startFreeAction`.
- Fate Itself can replace the shooter's own attack dice in a Shoot (the only window before re-rolls) and both fighters' dice in a Fight; an opponent's Shoot dice cannot be reached. A replacement die is tagged `wc.fate`, so `reclassify`, Rending and Punishing leave it alone; Severe is kept off it by moving tagged dice behind the rolled ones.
- The shared end-of-activation window runs before the `activation.end` hooks, so Capricious Plan resolves before Temporal Flux's return check.
- Echoes from the Warp shares the 2" counteract cap through the `moveLimitDelta` provider. The bot never plans Temporal Flux or a FLY move.

Shared-engine needs (none blocks the team): a defender window ahead of a Shoot's attack re-rolls (Fate Itself on the opponent's Shoot); a `reactions` entry point for the active seat (Savage Brutality as a reaction); a Severe conversion that skips tagged dice.

## 16. Farstalker Kinband

Rule IDs `T-FK.<n>`, checklist IDs `TEAM-FK-<nnn>`. Sources: the team PDF (Farstalker Kinband, faction version 3, June '26 update log state, including the June '26 rules commentary and the earlier errata it lists; the flow and layout extracts were read together) as the primary source, cross-checked against the Wahapedia page (faction version 3; its history lists June 2026 and a later July 2026 row, and every rule text we read matches the PDF's June '26 state) and its FAQ panel (one entry: Call the Kill with Blast or Torrent, the same answer as the PDF rules commentary). The two agree on every number; they differ in one place, the Hound's Bad-tempered, where Wahapedia puts the errata's order-change clause in the wrong sentence (16.3, UNCLEAR); the PDF wins. All rule text is restated in our own words; team, operative, weapon, ploy and equipment names are used as printed. Core terms per `10-rules-core.md` (R-x.y), missions and universal equipment per `11-missions.md` (M-x.y). Ploys and equipment are one bullet per record so each can carry its MECH line.

Weapon type column: R = ranged, M = melee. Dmg is `normal/crit`. Base is in mm.

### 16.1 Team selection

- T-FK.1 Roster is exactly 12 operatives: 1 KROOT KILL-BROKER (leader) plus 11 picks from the main list (T-FK.2). Nothing counts as two selections or half a selection.
  - MECH: roster validator: leader slot count 1 (`fk.kill-broker`), main slot count 11 | CLASS: data
- T-FK.2 Main list: BOW-HUNTER, COLD-BLOOD, CUT-SKIN, HEAVY GUNNER, HOUND, LONG-SIGHT, PISTOLIER, STALKER, TRACKER, WARRIOR. HOUND and WARRIOR may be taken more than once; at most two HOUNDs; every other entry at most once. Eight single cards plus two Hounds make ten, so every legal roster has at least one WARRIOR.
  - MECH: main slot `repeatable: ["fk.hound", "fk.warrior"]`, `selection.caps: [{ from: ["fk.hound"], max: 2 }]` | CLASS: data
- T-FK.3 Loadouts:
  - KILL-BROKER: ritual blade plus either the Kroot rifle (its 3+ profile) or the pulse weapon.
  - HEAVY GUNNER: blade plus either the Dvorgite skinner or the Londaxi tribalest.
  - WARRIOR: blade plus either the Kroot rifle (4+) or the Kroot scattergun.
  - BOW-HUNTER (accelerator bow, all three profiles, and blade), COLD-BLOOD (Kroot rifle 3+, blade), CUT-SKIN (Cut-skin's blades), HOUND (ripping fangs), LONG-SIGHT (Kroot hunting rifle, all three profiles, and blade), PISTOLIER (dual Kroot pistols, both profiles, and blade), STALKER (Kroot scattergun, Stalker's blade), TRACKER (Kroot rifle 4+, blade): fixed, no picker.

  - MECH: team.json `archetypes: ["infiltration", "recon"]` | CLASS: data
- T-FK.5 Keywords: every operative carries FARSTALKER KINBAND, T'AU EMPIRE and KROOT plus its role keyword (KILL-BROKER, BOW-HUNTER, COLD-BLOOD, CUT-SKIN, HEAVY GUNNER, HOUND, LONG-SIGHT, PISTOLIER, STALKER, TRACKER, WARRIOR); the Kill-Broker also has LEADER. T'AU EMPIRE is stored exactly as the Pathfinders store it (straight apostrophe), so any rule reading that keyword sees both teams. The PDF prints "FARSTALKER KINBAND ," with a stray space; the keyword is FARSTALKER KINBAND.

### 16.4 Operative rules and unique actions

- T-FK.7 **Call the Kill** (Kill-Broker): a STRATEGIC GAMBIT usable while the Kill-Broker is in the killzone. Pick one enemy operative anywhere in the killzone (no visibility or range) as your mark for the TP. Whenever a friendly FARSTALKER KINBAND operative shoots, fights or retaliates against the mark, its weapons have Balanced. Whenever the mark is incapacitated, you may pick another enemy operative as the new mark for the rest of the TP, and keep doing so each time a mark falls. The Kill-Broker need not be in the killzone for the re-pick.
  - MECH: 0 CP strategic gambit ability with an enemy pick (Combat Doctrine / Eye of the Ancestors pattern), gate "Kill-Broker in the killzone"; token `fk.callTheKill` (cap 1 per seat, `turningPointEnd`); `modifyWeaponRules` adds `core.wr.balanced` per `targetId`; the re-pick is a 0 CP offer in the `operative.killed` window (the FK seat, after removal) when the removed operative carried the token, with the pending fallback of 16.9 | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Farstalker Kinband Call the Kill new mark timing | the new mark is picked at the end of the action, after the incapacitated operatives are removed, for every way the mark can fall | the June '26 rules commentary (and Wahapedia FAQ) answers this for Blast and Torrent; one timing for all cases keeps the mark stable during an action | Confirmed
  - RULING: Farstalker Kinband Call the Kill pending re-pick | when no `operative.killed` window opens for the FK seat (the mark fell to its own Hot, a mine, direct damage, or a killer that fell in the same action), the re-pick and Victory Shriek wait as a 0 CP offer at the FK seat's next `firefight.activationStart`, `firefight.actionEnded` or `operative.killed` window in the same TP, and lapse at the TP's end | the engine opens the kill window only for a living killer of the other seat; the rule itself says "whenever the mark is incapacitated", whatever the cause | Unsourced
- T-FK.8 **Victory Shriek** (Kill-Broker): whenever your mark is incapacitated, you may pick one friendly FARSTALKER KINBAND operative within 6" of the Kill-Broker (no visibility); its weapons have Balanced for the rest of the battle. No operative can be picked for this more than once per battle.
  - MECH: offered together with the T-FK.7 re-pick (same window, a separate choice); token `fk.victoryShriek` (`expires: ['battle']`) on the picked operative; `modifyWeaponRules` adds Balanced while it carries the token; battle ledger of picked ids | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Farstalker Kinband Victory Shriek details | needs the Kill-Broker in the killzone when the pick is made (after removal, as T-FK.7); the 6" is measured then; the Kill-Broker may pick itself; a mark that fell only counts if Call the Kill set it this TP | the rule measures from the Kill-Broker, an operative is within any distance of itself (R-8.3), and only Call the Kill creates a mark | Unsourced
  - RULING: Farstalker Kinband Balanced from several sources | Balanced from Call the Kill, Victory Shriek and the Stalker's blade never stacks (one re-roll), and a weapon holding Balanced from any of them "already has Balanced" for Prey (T-FK.31) | a weapon rule is either present or not; Prey's own fallback clause exists because a second Balanced adds nothing | Unsourced
- T-FK.9 **ENERGISE** (Bow-Hunter, 1 AP): until the end of the TP, or until the Bow-Hunter has finished a Shoot action with its accelerator bow, every profile of the bow has Lethal 5+. Not while in an enemy's control range.
  - MECH: unique action setting an operative effect (`turningPointEnd`); `modifyWeaponRules` adds `core.wr.lethal` 5+ to `fk.wg.accelerator-bow` profiles; `action.ended` of a Shoot with a bow profile clears it | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Farstalker Kinband Energise expiry | the bonus lasts for the whole Shoot action that uses the bow (every voltaic Blast sequence keeps Lethal 5+) and ends when that action ends; a Guard interrupt Shoot with the bow also uses it up; fighting with the blade does not | "has shot" is complete only once the action is finished | Unsourced
- T-FK.10 **Hardy** (Cold-Blood): whenever an attack die would deal its Critical Dmg to the Cold-Blood, you may have it deal the weapon's Normal Dmg instead. Devastating and other non-die damage are untouched.
  - MECH: `onDamageInflicted` on this operative for sources `crit` and `strike-crit`: `amount = min(amount, normal Dmg of that weapon against it after modifiers)` (weapon from `weaponId`) | CLASS: team-hook

- T-FK.11 **Cold-blooded** (Cold-Blood): when it shoots, fights or retaliates against a wounded enemy operative, its weapons have Lethal 5+; if that enemy is also injured, they also have Rending.

### 16.9 Generic capabilities (survey; resolved in the Engine map below)

- **counteractAlternatives** (built, batch C): the FARSTALKER order change instead of counteracting. Used by T-FK.28.
- **extraTargets** (built): Salvo's second target. Used by T-FK.20.
- **weaponForbidden** (built): Concealed Position; the Hound's off-card weapons. Used by T-FK.14, T-FK.18.
- **fightTargets** (built): Bad-tempered's forced target; Savage Assault's same-enemy free Fight. Used by T-FK.13, T-FK.15.
- **markerActionRelief** (built): Poach's `contestSuffices`. Used by T-FK.35.
- Brief fallbacks used (not built, named in the brief): Quick Draw (the target-selection interrupt: 0 CP offer at `firefight.opponentActionDeclared`, T-FK.21); Ready-step decisions (0 CP offer in the gambit step, T-FK.27); a move with a marker action in the middle (Gather split, T-FK.17).
- **strikeOnly** (built in the batch C prep after this survey): an owed resolution from `fightResolveStart` / `afterFightResolution` with `strikeOnly: true` offers strikes only (mirror of `blockOnly`). Used by T-FK.23 (Stealth Attack).
- **anyKillWindow** (GAP, NICE): a window for the opposing seat whenever one of its marked enemies is incapacitated by any cause. `operative.killed` opens only for a living killer of the other seat after an attack, so the mark's Hot, a mine, direct damage (Vicious Duellist) or a killer that fell too open nothing. Fallback: Call the Kill re-pick and Victory Shriek wait as a pending 0 CP offer at the FK seat's next `firefight.activationStart`, `firefight.actionEnded` or `operative.killed` window in the TP (T-FK.7 RULING). Vengeance (T-FK.36) only fires on attack incapacitations (RULING).
- **fightRetained** (GAP, NICE): a fight hook with `engine` after both sides are retained (Punishing and Rending done) and before the first resolution. Vicious Duellist (T-FK.12) counts the enemy's discarded fails. Fallback: `afterAttackRoll` on the enemy's side (after re-rolls, before retention), predicting Punishing's fail-to-normal conversion.
- Everything else maps onto existing providers, hooks, windows and 0 CP offers (Engine map).

### 16.10 Gotchas

- Roster is 12 operatives (1 + 11): up to two Hounds, any number of Warriors, everything else once; a legal roster always has at least one Warrior. Twelve operatives use the 12-operative kill grade row.
- Two Kroot rifles: 3+ (Kill-Broker, Cold-Blood) and 4+ (Tracker, Warrior); both are "Kroot rifle" for Piercing Shot and Toxin Shot. The Kroot hunting rifle is not.
- The Farstalker faction rule has two halves: a Ready-step order change for up to three operatives (offered in the gambit step), and an order change instead of counteracting that passes the turn without spending that operative's counteract.
- Call the Kill is a gambit only while the Kill-Broker is in the killzone; the mark is public, lasts the TP, and a fallen mark is replaced after the action (FAQ). Victory Shriek needs the Kill-Broker in the killzone and each operative only once per battle. Balanced never stacks; Prey turns an already-Balanced ranged weapon into Ceaseless + Severe.
- The Hound is a Beast: no Shoot, no mission or equipment actions, no grenades; it can Guard and GATHER. Bad-tempered has two halves: forcing an enemy Fight onto the Hound (declaration offer) and a free Charge reaction when an enemy charges a friend within 3" of it.
- Cut-Skin: Vicious Duellist is direct damage per enemy fail and can end the fight before any strike; Savage Assault is a second free Fight against the same enemy only, in its own activation only.
- Stalker charges under Conceal; STEALTH ATTACK needs a Conceal order, 1" from Light or Heavy terrain, no enemy in control range; Move only (no +2"); the first strike is followed at once by another strike.
- Long-Sight: the concealed profile is only for its first Shoot of the battle; both Heavy profiles forbid moving in that activation; LONG-SIGHT lasts until its next activation (through counteractions) and denies obscured to any hunting-rifle profile.
- Pistolier: Salvo shoots two different primary targets as separate sequences; Quick Draw is once per TP, needs the Pistolier ready, and in our build is offered when the enemy declares Shoot.
- Tracker's Pech'ra has no range limit and gives Seek Light against enemies within 1" of it (visible); it goes when the Tracker next activates.
- Rogue strips Saturate and gives one cover improvement that does not stack with Vantage; Cut-Throats caps melee Atk at 5; Bound saves 2" on one climb per activation; Slip Away makes Fall Back 1 AP (so a legal counteraction).
- Meat and Trophy exclude the Hound; Ready for Anything (Warriors only) is a separate once-per-TP use of Meat, Piercing Shot or Toxin Shot.
- Edition leaks to reject: nothing from the 2021 book (shape distances, Overwatch, older datacards, ploys or tac ops), no 40k 10th Kroot rules (datasheet abilities, scout moves, wound rolls, invulnerable saves); inches only, three defence dice, every printed number from the June '26 cards.

## 17. Imperial Navy Breachers

Rule IDs `T-NB.<n>`, checklist IDs `TEAM-NB-<nnn>`. Sources: the Imperial Navy Breachers team PDF (Kill Team 2024, Faction version 3, August '26 update log state; the flow and layout extracts were read together) as the primary source, cross-checked against the Wahapedia page (faction version 3, August 2026; its FAQ panel is empty for this team) and the core rules page for terms. The two agree on every stat line and weapon profile; Wahapedia lags the August '26 errata in three places (listed in 17.10), and the PDF errata wins there. Facts read from the PDF are Confirmed; our own calls are Unsourced. All rule text is restated in our own words; team, operative, weapon, ploy and equipment names are used as printed. Core terms per `10-rules-core.md` (R-x.y), missions and universal equipment per `11-missions.md` (M-x.y). Ploys and equipment are one bullet per record so each can carry its MECH line.

We play only the open Volkus killzone. Every clause that needs hatchways, Wall terrain or close quarters (Operate Hatch, Weld Shut, System Override Device, the hatch half of Deck Hand) has a RULING "no effect in the open killzone"; Accessible terrain does exist in the open killzone (building doorways, Breach markers), so the Accessible clauses still work.

Weapon type column: R = ranged, M = melee. Dmg is `normal/crit`. Base is in mm.

No CP is spent.

### 17.9 Generic capabilities (survey; resolved in the Engine map below)

Every rule maps onto the batch A, B and C layers except these, each built team-local:
- **ignoreAplDecreases** (gap): Rebreathers ignores APL changes at the player's option, so only decreases. `flags.ignoreApl` drops every change, positives included (and `applyAplEffect` refuses new ones), which would cancel Wayfind and Overwhelm Target. Fallback: team code removes negative `aplFx` entries from friendly Breachers in `action.ended` and `activation.start` handlers (RULING T-NB.41).
- **operativeIntervening** (gap): Breachwall needs "is this operative intervening" between a shooter and a target; `los.interveningTraits` covers terrain only. Fallback: team-local top-down segment-versus-disc test from sampled points of the shooter's base to the facing half of the target's base (RULING T-NB.19).
- **wholeModelViewpoint** (gap, listed in the brief): C.A.T. Unit visibility from any part of the model. Fallback: head point (RULING T-NB.16).
- **ploySwap** (gap, listed in the brief): Command Breach turns one strategy ploy into the other. Fallback: `effects.removeEffects` then add the other ploy's effect and switch the marker kind.
- **optionalChain** (minor): `chainActivation` owes the activation, while Breach and Clear says "can". Fallback: the opt-in is the partner pick (RULING T-NB.32).

### 17.10 Gotchas

- PDF wins over Wahapedia in three places, each with a Corrected RULING: GUNNER is exempt from the once-each limit (two Gunners, same weapon allowed); Deck Hand needs APL 1 or 2; Overwhelm Target lets you pick either operative of the pair. The PDF's own selection page also still prints the old Gunner text; the update log wins.
- Eleven operatives, not ten: the Sergeant plus 10 selections. C.A.T. Unit and Gheistskull share one selection, need the Surveyor / Void-Jammer, and are Expendable (no kill op value either way).
- Machines have no weapons, cannot retaliate or assist, count APL -1 for control, and cannot be picked as a target on Conceal in cover beyond 2" (Seek and Vantage do not help). The C.A.T. Unit also cannot climb or jump, cannot act or activate in an enemy's control range or after its Surveyor dies, and so can never Fall Back. The Gheistskull does not fly.
- Group Activation is mandatory and stops at two Armsmen; it is switched off for both members of a Breach and Clear pair. Breach and Clear is once per TP and the partner must be visible and within 3" when picked.
- Command Breach: Attack/Defence Order cost 0 CP only while the Sergeant is in the killzone; the in-activation move or swap is once per Sergeant activation, one option only, and never in a counteraction.
- Void Armour re-rolls only against Blast or Torrent weapons with no sweeping profile, two dice for the Grenadier; separately, x" Devastating cannot hurt a friendly Breacher that is not the sequence's target.
- Brace for Counterattack reduces Normal and Critical Dmg of 3+ only (never Devastating), needs the operative in your territory or unmoved by Charge/Fall Back/Reposition this TP; Dash does not count. Emboldened runs after it on the reduced value.
- Close Assault is not for retaliating; its Dmg bonus is for Navis shotguns and heavy shotguns, its fail-to-normal clause for any weapon. Slugs are for the Navis shotgun (long range) only, three per TP across the team.
- Detonate: the Gheistskull is always the primary target (no cover, no obscured, no visibility needed), Blast 1" also hits friends, Lethal 4+ and Stun, one use per battle; the weapon cannot be picked without the Gheistskull in the killzone. Boost is once per battle, never in TP1, and only boosts a Charge later in the same activation.
- The Endurant is Move 4", Save 2+, 11 wounds; Disengage makes its Fall Back 1 AP (counteract-legal); Shield makes each block cancel two successes; Breachwall needs Engage, intervening, and exactly one other friendly base touching.
- Rebreathers ignores only APL decreases (keep Wayfind, Overwhelm Target) and switches off enemy Shock. Combat Stimms restores Move, not Hit.
- Open killzone only: Weld Shut, System Override Device and Deck Hand's hatch half do nothing; Breach Point and Deck Hand's Accessible crossing still work.
- Edition leaks to reject: no 2021 Breacher rules (no 2021 Gheistskull or C.A.T. profiles, no Overwatch, no shape distances), no 40k 10th mechanics (no wound rolls, no invulnerable or void shield saves); inches only, three defence dice, every printed number from the August '26 cards.

## Teams added in M10 batch D (Blooded, Fellgor Ravagers, Chaos Cult, Goremongers, Scout Squad, Tempestus Aquilons, Exaction Squad)

Sections 18 to 24 use the layout of sections 11 to 17 (MECH and CLASS lines, survey, gotchas, Engine map, Implementer
brief). The batch D engine prep built the shared capabilities below (`00-architecture.md` section 11, row M10 batch D
prep, tests GEN-099 to GEN-110 in `tests/engine/generic-e.test.ts`); every team keeps using the batch A, B and C
layers listed above. The implementer rules above apply unchanged, with id prefixes `bl.`, `fg.`, `cc.`, `gm.`, `ss.`,
`ta.`, `ex.` and figure prefixes `bl-`, `fg-`, `cc-`, `gm-`, `ss-`, `ta-`, `ex-` (v2 concept slugs
`<prefix><operative>[-<loadout or variant>]`, one body per loadout in the client file's `loadoutBodies`, every
archetype in `standIns` until its GLB is in the manifest). Each team is scaffolded behind `"playable": false` with its
leader datacard and the leader's weapons only.

Survey result: of the guessed gaps, two needed a shared capability (Chaos Cult mutation, Tempestus Aquilons whole-batch
deployment above the killzone) and the rest fit the existing layer. The Blooded token economy is a pool plus a token
(`pools.ts`, `tokens.ts`) driven by a 0 CP gambit; Goremongers blood is a capped token; Fellgor frenzy is team hooks on
top of the new kill log; the Exaction Cyber-mastiff is a joint activation (`joinActivation`) with team bans; Scout
Squad infiltration is the new pre-battle step. What did need a shared capability:

| Capability | Where | What it gives a team |
|---|---|---|
| Change of datacard (transformOperative) | `src/engine/transform.ts` (`transformOperative(ctx, opId, toCardId, { keepWoundsLost?, loadout? })`, `transformProblem`); event `OperativeTransformed`; datacard field `selectable: false` (data and runtime), snapshotted with its team (`bundle.snapshotData`), accepted by validate-data outside every slot; client feed line, the figure follows the new card | Chaos Cult Mutation: Devotee to Mutant to Torment mid-battle, keeping id, order, readiness, the activation in progress, APL effects, tokens, picks and equipment weapons; wounds lost carry over (never below 1); a bigger base that no longer fits moves to the nearest legal spot within 6" |
| Kill log (killLog) | `src/engine/kills.ts` (`state.kills: KillRecord[]`, `killsSince`, `lastKillOf`, `scoreAsIncapacitated`); `Operative.incapacitatedBy` set in `inflict`; lifecycle hook `operative.removed` (`OperativeRemovedData { killerId, cause }`, cause `attack`, `direct`, `offboard` or `scored`), run once per removal from the per-step removal pass | kills of any cause with their killer (Reward Earned, Mutation after a kill, Marked for Justice, gore and token gains); Frenzy counts for the kill op while the operative stays (`scoreAsIncapacitated`; the later removal is not counted or logged again). Decisions after a kill go to the next reaction point; the `operative.killed` ploy window still covers attack kills only |
| Re-roll value bans (rerollBannedValues) | provider `rerollBannedValues(state, { kind, rollerId, opponentId, defence })`; `attack-common.banGrantValues` narrows the grants `attackStats` / `defenceStats` return (odds and the default policy follow), `rerollBannedFor` filters the Command Re-roll and `parseReroll` refuses | Sinister Trophies, Strobing Phosphor-lumen: attack dice showing 1 cannot be re-rolled |
| Pre-battle choices (preBattleChoices) | provider `preBattleChoices(state, seat)`; setup step `preBattle` after the last operative is set up and before TP1; one `ability.choice` with `context.preBattle` at a time, seats alternating from the setup initiative holder, a pass ends that seat; the offer's code hook calls `setup.preBattleChoiceDone(ctx)`; a free action started there (`startFreeAction`) calls it from its frame resume | Scout Squad Forward Scouting (free Reposition, picks), Tempestus Aquilons Drop markers, Blooded Regular Dosage |
| APL decreases ignored, live flags | provider `flags` may return `ignoreAplDecreases` (`OperativeFlags.ignoreAplDecreases`, read by `effectiveApl`: only increases count); `refreshFlags` now runs after every accepted step (`apply.afterAction`), so position-based `flags` are current; the two local APL sums in `abilities.ts` now call `effectiveApl` | Mirror-visor, Engendered Focus, Toxic Blessings; Gruelling Disciplinarian's ignore-injury aura |
| Extra cover saves only (extraCoverSaves) | provider `extraCoverSaves(state, op)` read in the shared `afterDefenceRoll` handler after Stealthy | Blooded and Scout Squad Camo Cloak (one more cover save, never a crit) |
| One-seat markers | `Marker.pickableBy?: Seat` (`markers.markerOffers`) | Goremongers Bloody Cadaver |
| Charge mid-action window | window `firefight.chargeMoved` (the mover's owner, between a Charge's move and the end of the action; resume `charge.moved`), the twin of `firefight.fallBackMoved` | Goremongers Rake, Blooded Avalanche of Muscle |
| Before-damage shoot window | window `shoot.beforeResolve` (both seats, attacker first) after blocks and before any damage of the sequence; `AttackSequence.unblocked { normal, crit }` holds what will inflict damage and may be lowered; damage is now dealt in shoot step `resolve` | Goremongers Drag (pull, then discard unblocked successes), Impending Apotheosis |
| Whole-batch set-aside (setAsideBatches) | provider `setAsideBatches(state, seat) -> { skipFirst? }`; `SetupState.batches`, `deploy.aside`; the batch's first answer decides; a batch going aside offers no deployment (`context.wholeBatchAside`, empty `constraints.operativeIds`) and refuses one; the shared AI sets aside the rest of such a batch | Tempestus Aquilons Drop Insertion (batches two and three may go above, never the first) |
| Spots on raised floors | `SpotOpts.levels` (also sample terrain floors) and `SpotOpts.notUnderVantage` in `reserve.placementSpots` | Tempestus Aquilons landing on Vantage; transform re-placement |

Not built (each section's survey names the team-local fallback and its RULING): an interrupting activation (Execution
Order), a window after the weapon pick (`shoot.weaponSelected`: Long Arm, Special Issue Shells), reactions before
removal for causes other than attacks (Gunfight, Destructive Demise, Explosive and Bitter Demise outside attacks),
counteract ploys with a cost (Gorethirst), a move through enemy control range (Cleaver Flurry, done with a team path),
a strike owed by an incapacitated fighter (Wretched), ending an attack sequence for both sides (Frenzy, done with team
damage hooks), per-die defender choices (Vile Blessing, Impending Apotheosis in fights), a veto on ending an
activation (forced landing), per-batch set-up decisions beyond the pre-battle step, move truncation on a team mine
(Booby Trap), loadout stat changes (Assault Shield: set `op.save` at set-up), a stun-test hook (Pox Bomb), thrown melee
weapons as Shoot weapons (Wrist Chains: `ownGrenades.weapons` twin records), and activation choices that are not
actions (Guidance and Experience: a 0 AP unique action). None blocks a team. The shared AI still lands operatives only
through `/emerge/` actions and sets aside per operative under a third cap (`src/ai/setup.ts`, `moves.ts`): the Tempestus
Aquilons implementer extends both for `ta.a.land` and whole batches.

## 18. Blooded

Rule IDs `T-BL.<n>`, checklist IDs `TEAM-BL-<nnn>`. Sources: the Blooded team PDF (Kill Team 2024, Faction version 3, April '26, including its update log with the April '26 errata and the previous errata; the flow and layout extracts were read together) as the primary source, cross-checked against the Wahapedia Blooded page (faction version 3, April 2026; its FAQ panel is empty for this team), plus the core rules page for terms. Facts read from the PDF are Confirmed; our own calls are Unsourced. The two sources agree on every stat line, weapon profile and base size; in one place the PDF's update log says more than both card texts (Glory Kill, T-BL.36) and we apply the update log. All rule text is restated in our own words; team, operative, weapon, ploy and equipment names are used as printed. Core terms per `10-rules-core.md` (R-x.y), missions and universal equipment per `11-missions.md` (M-x.y). Ploys and equipment are one bullet per record so each can carry its MECH line.

Weapon type column: R = ranged, M = melee. Dmg is `normal/crit`. Base is in mm.

### 18.5 Faction rules

- T-BL.33 **BLOODED: gaining tokens**. Your Blooded tokens are a team resource. You gain one unassigned token (a) in the Ready step of each Strategy phase, (b) the first time each TP that an enemy operative is incapacitated (any cause), and (c) the first time each TP that a friendly operative is incapacitated while within 6" of an enemy operative. Gains from T-BL.12, T-BL.18 and T-BL.42 are also unassigned; T-BL.8 returns one.
  - MECH: pool `bl.blooded` (`pools.gainPool`, HUD chip label "Blooded"); (a) hook `turningPoint.start`; (b) and (c) hook `operative.removed` (batch D killLog: every cause) with TP ledgers `bl.gain.enemy` / `bl.gain.friendly`; (c) measures from the removed operative's last position | CLASS: generic:killLog (pool existing)
  - RULING: Blooded token gains | any cause counts (Hot, mines, Bitter Demise and Explosive Demise included); a friendly operative incapacitated within 6" of an enemy counts even if its own team did it; the token arrives when the operative is removed | the card names no cause; removal follows incapacitation within the same action (R-5.18) | Unsourced
- T-BL.34 **BLOODED gambit**: once per Strategy phase, as a STRATEGIC GAMBIT (no CP), assign any number of your unassigned tokens to friendly BLOODED operatives that hold none (one token per operative at most). Then, if four or more friendly operatives in the killzone hold a token, you may pick one of them to be under the Gaze of the Gods until the end of the TP. An assigned token stays on its operative for the battle; it is lost when the operative is removed (unless T-BL.8).
  - MECH: 0 CP strategy record `bl.p.blooded` in `strategy.gambit` (the Doctrina / Skill at Arms pattern); its code hook loops `ability.choice` (assign one token to an eligible operative, or stop) moving one from the pool (`spendPool`) to the operative (`tokens.addToken` kind `bl.blooded`, cap 1, expiry battle), then, with four or more holders, `ability.choice` for the Gaze (token `bl.gaze`, expiry `turningPointEnd`), then `resumeGambit` | CLASS: team-hook (pool and tokens existing)
  - RULING: Blooded gambit use | usable with no unassigned tokens (to pick a Gaze only); tokens never leave an operative except at removal; the Gaze pick is optional, the AI always makes it (preferring the Chieftain or the best melee operative) and always assigns every token it can | the card gives tokens no expiry and makes both steps permissive ("can") | Unsourced
- T-BL.35 **BLOODED: token effects**. A token holder's weapons have Accurate 1. If it is also under the Gaze, one of the normal successes it retains through that Accurate 1 is retained as a crit instead.
  - MECH: `modifyAttackDice` pushes 1 to `accurate` for holders (shoot and fight, retaliating included); `afterAttackRoll` (also in queries) turns one die tagged `accurate` into a crit when `underGaze` holds (not for an obscured shoot sequence) | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Gaze crit and combined Accurate | when Accurate 1 combines with another instance into Accurate 2 (R-10.1), still only one retained die becomes a crit; against an obscured target it stays a normal success | the rule converts "one of your normal successes"; R-5.8 stops crits while obscured | Confirmed

### 18.6 Ploys

The source prints no costs: every ploy is 1 CP (R-2.4) unless a rule changes it (T-BL.44). Strategy ploys last until the end of the TP (R-2.5).

- T-BL.36 **GLORY KILL** | Strategy | 1 CP | Gambit step | Pick one enemy operative visible to a friendly BLOODED operative. For the TP, a friendly BLOODED operative shooting, fighting or retaliating against it has Ceaseless on its weapons, or Relentless instead if it is a token holder.

- T-BL.38 **MALEVOLENT GRIT** | Strategy | 1 CP | Gambit step | When an operative shoots a friendly BLOODED operative that is a token holder or wholly within your opponent's territory, you may re-roll one defence die.
  - MECH: `modifyDefenceDice` adds `RerollGrant { mode: 'one' }` | CLASS: team-hook
- T-BL.39 **BITTER DEMISE** | Strategy | 1 CP | Gambit step | For the TP, when a friendly BLOODED operative is incapacitated, before it is removed, roll a D3: on a 3 (2+ if it is a token holder) deal damage equal to the result to one enemy operative visible to and within 2" of it.
  - MECH: hook `operative.incapacitated` while the effect is active; the D3 is rolled only when an enemy qualifies; in an attack's removal queue the enemy pick is an `ability.choice` (continueRemovals afterwards); outside attacks the team picks; `effects.directDamage` | CLASS: team-hook

- T-BL.40 **CALLOUS DISREGARD** | Firefight | 1 CP | A friendly BLOODED operative performs Shoot, as targets are chosen | For that action, friendly operatives in an enemy's control range do not stop that enemy being a valid target. Until the action ends, each attack die you discard as a fail deals damage equal to its result to one friendly operative of your choice within the target's control range.

### 18.10 Gotchas

- Roster is 1 + 9 + 4 selections: 12 to 14 operatives, so the 12, 13 and 14 kill grade rows are used. Enforcer and Ogryn weigh 2 in the heavy slot and are each once only; Troopers may come from both lists. Gunners plus Sharpshooter at most three; each Gunner weapon once; only one plasma weapon in the whole kill team (plasma gun Gunner or Chieftain plasma pistol).
- Every card is APL 2, the Chieftain included. The Chieftain's bayonet is Hit 3+, everyone else's 4+. Gunner weapons are Hit 4+ (not the Kasrkin 3+). Diabolyk bomb 4/3 and meltagun 6/3 as printed.
- Two token places: the unassigned pool (HUD chip) and at most one token on each operative. Tokens are assigned only in the Blooded gambit; everything that gains a token mid-turn adds to the pool. Assigned tokens last the battle and vanish with their operative (Blooded Icon returns one per TP).
- Gaze needs four or more holders in the killzone at gambit time and lasts the TP. The Gaze crit converts one Accurate-retained die; Lead With Strength gives the Chieftain the Gaze but not a token.
- A Name Whispered In Blood treats the Sharpshooter as a holder under the Gaze only while it shoots its chosen enemy; it never counts for the four-holder test.
- Reckless Aspirant: Accurate 1 for non-holders only when shooting or fighting (not retaliating); Punishing for holders whenever. Glory Kill: Ceaseless, or Relentless for holders; the pick must be visible to a friendly BLOODED operative (update log).
- Group Activation is mandatory and links every BLOODED TROOPER (both lists), two in a row at most.
- Gruelling Disciplinarian is live by distance (batch D flag refresh) plus a per-activation memory; Chem-enhanced ignores every APL change, so Signal cannot pick the Ogryn and Moment of Repute does nothing for it.
- Explosive Demise hurts friends too and is optional; Bitter Demise rolls a D3 and needs an enemy within 2"; Callous Disregard spills each fail onto your own operatives near the target.
- Camo Cloak here is one extra cover save only (no crit, no Saturate immunity), unlike the Kasrkin and Angels of Death cards.
- Slow-witted makes Pick Up Marker and mission actions 2 AP for the Ogryn (Operate Hatch excepted), so ENFORCE cannot hand it one.
- Edition leaks to reject: nothing from the 2021 Blooded or Traitor Guard cards (no Overwatch, no shape distances, no 2021 Chaos Blessings or Gift tables), nothing from 40k 10th Chaos or Astra Militarum (no Orders, no Leadership or battle-shock tests, no Dark Pacts, no wound rolls or AP); inches only, three defence dice, every printed number from the April '26 cards.

## 19. Fellgor Ravagers

Rule IDs `T-FG.<n>`, checklist IDs `TEAM-FG-<nnn>`. Sources: the Fellgor Ravagers team PDF (Kill Team 2024, faction version 3, August '26 update log state: the August '26 errata and rules commentary, plus the previous errata and commentary; the flow and layout extracts were read together) as the primary source, cross-checked against the Wahapedia Fellgor Ravager page (faction version 3, August 2026; its FAQ block has one entry, Violent Temperament against re-rolled or replaced dice). The PDF's update log also answers a second question (a crit with Critical Dmg 0 cannot finish off a Frenzy operative), which Wahapedia lacks. The two sources agree on every stat line and weapon profile, and both already carry the August '26 changes (Mangler Hit 4+, Gnarlscar and Mangler Wounds 10, Tech-curse Seek Light, Gong Knell without the Piercing clause, Incite Fury without SUPPORT). In two places the "previous errata" list says more than the current card (Ambush, Reckless Determination); both cards and Wahapedia print the shorter text, so the current card wins (19.10). Facts read from the PDF are Confirmed; our own calls are Unsourced. All rule text is restated in our own words; team, operative, weapon, ploy and equipment names are used as printed. Core terms per `10-rules-core.md` (R-x.y), missions and universal equipment per `11-missions.md` (M-x.y). Ploys and equipment are one bullet per record so each can carry its MECH line.

Weapon type column: R = ranged, M = melee. Dmg is `normal/crit`. Base is in mm.

### 19.4 Operative rules and unique actions

- T-FG.7 **Call the Attack** (Ironhorn, STRATEGIC GAMBIT): usable while the Ironhorn is in the killzone and not frenzied. Pick one friendly FELLGOR RAVAGER operative visible to and within 6" of the Ironhorn (the Ironhorn itself allowed). That operative and every other friendly FELLGOR RAVAGER operative visible to and within 2" of it may each perform a free Dash, in the order you choose.
  - MECH: Strategy-phase gambit with an operative choice (Combat Doctrine pattern), gated on `fg.ironhorn` active and not frenzied; the group is fixed at use; `startFreeSequence` of optional free Dashes in the player's order (strategy free moves, `ReactionInfo.strategy`) | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Call the Attack group | the Ironhorn may pick itself (it is within 6" of itself, R-8.3); the 2" group is fixed when the gambit is used; each Dash is optional and follows the Dash rules (3", no climbing); a frenzied operative may be picked or swept along | the card restricts only the Ironhorn's own Frenzy state; the Relocate precedent (T-KS.29) fixes the group at use | Unsourced
- T-FG.8 **Icon Bearer** (Deathknell): Frenzy's control bullet (T-FG.30 e) never applies to the Deathknell, and when control of a marker is worked out its APL counts 1 higher. This is not a change to its APL stat, so it adds to any APL changes it has.
  - MECH: provider `controlApl` returns `apl + 1` for `fg.deathknell` (markers only), and the Frenzy branch of the same provider skips it | CLASS: team-hook

### 19.5 Faction rules

- T-FG.29 **FRENZY: gaining it**: whenever a friendly FELLGOR RAVAGER operative without a Frenzy token would be incapacitated, from any cause, it is not incapacitated; instead it gains one of your Frenzy tokens, every remaining attack die in that sequence is discarded (in a fight, both fighters' dice), and if it has a Conceal order it changes to Engage. The opponent counts it as incapacitated at that moment (T-FG.32).
  - MECH: `beforeIncapacitated` handler: `data.wounds = 1` (the Frenzy floor), `addToken(fg.frenzy)` (owner = the Fellgor seat, no expiry), order to Engage with `OrderChanged`, `scoreAsIncapacitated(ctx, op.id, attackerId)` (killer = the attacker when it is an enemy, else null). Remaining dice (endSequence fallback): in a fight every unresolved die of both sides is marked `used`, so the fight ends; in a Shoot a per-sequence effect `fg.frenzyCut` (keyed to the attack and target index) zeroes every later damage to that operative in the sequence through `onDamageInflicted`, and those dice are ignored by the Frenzy counters | CLASS: generic:scoreAsIncapacitated + team-hook (gap: endSequence, not built in batch D)
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy wounds | a frenzied operative is held at 1 wound in the engine; its true state is the token, and damage never takes it below 1 except through T-FG.31 | the card gives no wound count; 0 wounds means incapacitated everywhere in the engine | Unsourced
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy causes | any incapacitation triggers it: enemy dice, Devastating, Hot, mines, direct damage, and friendly damage (Sweeping Blow, Gore Marks) | "would be incapacitated during the battle" names no source | Confirmed
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy discard | in a Shoot the dice still waiting to deal damage to that operative deal none (Devastating already resolved stays); in a fight the fight ends with nothing more resolved by either side | "all remaining attack dice are discarded, including yours if fighting or retaliating" | Confirmed
- T-FG.30 **FRENZY: while frenzied**, an operative:
  - (a) is incapacitated only as T-FG.31 says;
  - (b) cannot have a Conceal order;
  - (c) is injured (Warrior excepted, T-FG.28);
  - (d) cannot perform Pick Up Marker, unique actions (except SWEEPING BLOW) or mission actions (except Operate Hatch);
  - (e) counts as APL 1 for control of markers and areas, whatever its APL changes are (Deathknell excepted, T-FG.8).
  - MECH: (b) provider `orders` returns `['engage']`; (c) provider `injuredEquivalent` true (not for Warriors); (d) provider `actionForbidden` for `marker:pickUp`, every `ability:<id>` that is not `fg.a.sweeping-blow` and not an Operate Hatch action (grenade and equipment actions included); (e) provider `controlApl` returns 1 | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy unique actions | equipment and grenade actions (Stun Grenade, Smoke Grenade, the Pox Bomb copy) count as unique actions and are barred | 2024 rules call every non-universal, non-mission action a unique action | Unsourced
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy control | APL 1 for control even for the Toxhorn (Toxic Blessings covers APL changes, not this control rule) | the control bullet takes precedence over stat changes by its own words | Confirmed
- T-FG.31 **FRENZY: how a frenzied operative dies**: only when one of these happens (every other damage to it is ignored):
  - (a) its activation or counteraction ends;
  - (b) an enemy fighting or retaliating against it strikes it with a critical success (whose Critical Dmg is above 0);
  - (c) an enemy fighting or retaliating against it strikes it with a normal success for the second time since it gained the token (the two may come from different Fight actions and different enemies);
  - (d) an enemy shooting it inflicts Critical Dmg on it;
  - (e) an enemy shooting it inflicts Normal Dmg from two or more attack dice in that sequence;
  - (f) the battle ends (before any end-of-battle victory conditions).
  - MECH: `onDamageInflicted` on a frenzied FELLGOR RAVAGER: sources `strike-crit` (b) and `crit` (d) pass through when `amount > 0`; `strike-normal` (c) increments the per-operative counter `fg.normalStrikes` and passes only on the second; `normal` (e) increments a per-sequence counter and passes only on the second; everything else (`devastating`, `hot`, `direct`, and damage cut by `fg.frenzyCut`) is set to 0. A passed amount takes the operative from 1 to 0 and `inflict` incapacitates it normally. (a) `activation.end` (`data.counteract` included) and (f) `turningPoint.end` of the last TP kill it through `directDamage` under a one-shot `fg.frenzyKill` effect that the damage handler lets through, then `queueRemoval` | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy kill thresholds | a strike or die counts only if its damage after every reduction (War Gong, Toxic Blessings, enemy rules) is above 0, matching the update log answer on Critical Dmg 0; a War Gong-converted shooting crit counts as Normal Dmg (e), while a crit strike in a fight still counts as (b) | the update log rules out a 0 Critical Dmg crit; War Gong changes the damage, not the success | Unsourced
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy shooting count | the two dice in (e) must come from the same shooting sequence; a Blast or Torrent secondary is its own sequence; dice from separate Shoot actions do not add up | "an enemy operative is shooting it and Normal Dmg from two or more attack dice is inflicted" describes one shooting | Unsourced
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy end of activation | gaining the token in its own activation or counteraction means it dies when that ends; gained during the enemy's turn, it lives until its next activation or counteraction ends; a Strategy phase free Dash is not an activation | the card's first condition | Confirmed
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy battle end | resolved in the last TP's `turningPoint.end`, before that TP's crit op scoring and the end-of-battle kill op comparison; the opponent already counted it (T-FG.32), so nothing is counted twice | the card puts it before victory conditions that resolve at the end of the battle | Confirmed
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy odds | the engine's displayed odds treat a frenzied target as an operative on 1 wound (they overstate the kill chance from a single Normal Dmg die); the target's tooltip names Frenzy | a kill model for alternate incapacitation is not built in batch D | Unsourced
- T-FG.32 **FRENZY: scored as incapacitated**: the opponent treats a Fellgor operative as incapacitated when it gains its Frenzy token, not when it later dies: for VP (kill op) and for faction rules that need an incapacitation (Hand of the Archon Power From Pain, Chaos Cult Mutation and the like).

  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Frenzy scoring reach | other teams' rules that read `operative.removed` or the kill log see the token gain as the kill; ploy windows that open only on an attack removal (`operative.killed`) do not open then, nor at the later real removal | the card covers VP and faction rules; the shared kill log is the one place those rules read | Unsourced

### 19.6 Ploys

The source prints no costs: every ploy is 1 CP (R-2.4) unless a rule changes it (T-FG.41). Strategy ploys last until the end of the TP (R-2.5).

- T-FG.33 **VIOLENT TEMPERAMENT** | Strategy | 1 CP | Gambit step | When a friendly FELLGOR RAVAGER operative fights or retaliates, after its attack dice are rolled, you may re-roll all of them (all or none). Dice the opponent already re-rolled or replaced are left alone (update log commentary).
  - MECH: 0 CP offer in the `fight.beforeRerolls` window for the Fellgor fighter while the ploy is in effect; `attack-common.forcedReroll` over every die that is not already re-rolled and not a fixed die (`isFixedDie`) | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Violent Temperament | offered once per fighter per sequence, before any other re-roll; the re-rolled dice cannot be re-rolled again (R-9.2), so a Command Re-roll or Gore Marks can then only touch dice it left alone | "after rolling your attack dice ... re-roll all" sets the moment; the commentary excludes dice already changed | Confirmed
- T-FG.34 **AMBUSH** | Strategy | 1 CP | Gambit step | A friendly FELLGOR RAVAGER operative whose order changes from Conceal to Engage when it is activated is ambushing for that activation. While an ambushing operative fights (not retaliates), you may retain one of its normal successes as a critical success. A frenzied operative cannot ambush.
  - MECH: `activation.start` with `data.previousOrder = conceal`, `data.order = engage` while the ploy is in effect sets effect `fg.ambush` (expires `activation`), dropped if the operative gains a Frenzy token; `afterAttackRoll` (fight, attacker side) converts one `normal` to `crit` | CLASS: team-hook
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Ambush errata | only the normal-to-crit option; the older "retain a fail as a normal" alternative is not applied | the current card (August '26) and Wahapedia print only normal-to-crit; the update log's previous-errata text predates the current card | Confirmed
  - RULING: Fellgor Ravagers Ambush use | the conversion is automatic (a crit is never worse than a normal in a fight); only in the operative's own activation, not counteractions or free-action frames outside it | "is activated" names the activation | Unsourced

### 19.10 Gotchas

- Current card over the update log's previous errata twice (Confirmed): Ambush is normal-to-crit only; Reckless Determination needs "cannot retain any cover saves". The August '26 errata are already on both sources' cards: Mangler Hit 4+, Gnarlscar and Mangler W10, Tech-curse Seek Light, Gong Knell is Save +1 only, Incite Fury is not SUPPORT, Frenzy's fifth incapacitation condition (two Normal Dmg dice) exists, Call the Attack is a STRATEGIC GAMBIT barred to a frenzied Ironhorn.
- Frenzy is the spine and touches everything: a frenzied operative sits on 1 wound in the engine, ignores all damage except the six T-FG.31 conditions, dies when its own activation or counteraction ends, is Engage only, is injured (not the Warrior), uses APL 1 for control (not the Deathknell) and can only perform Sweeping Blow among unique actions. The opponent's kill op counts it at token gain (D2), so its later death is never counted again.
- The Frenzy damage handler must run after every other Fellgor reduction (War Gong first, then Toxic Blessings, then Frenzy) and must treat zero-damage dice as not counting (update log commentary).
- "Fighting" is not "retaliating": Ambush, Vicious Blows, Tactual Hunter and Ruthless Rampage are fighting-only; Blade Whirl, Violent Temperament, Animalistic Fury, Gore Marks and Frenzy's fight conditions cover both.
- Mangler: no Shoot at all (Guard only to Fight), +1 AP for Pick Up Marker and mission actions, a free second Fight once per activation (Savage), and Ruthless Rampage cannot come between the two Fights.
- Whip Control affects the enemy whoever it fights and makes Fall Back cost 1 extra AP; Incite Fury cannot pick a Shaman or the Ironhorn, nor itself.
- Sweeping Blow and Pox Bomb hurt friendly operatives too (Sweeping Blow deals damage, Pox Bomb only stuns friends); Sweeping Blow can push a friend into Frenzy.
- Gore Marks damage can trigger Frenzy mid-fight and end the fight before its re-roll.
- Pelting Firepower reads the whole TP's shooting history, written even before the ploy is used.
- Operate Hatch exceptions (Frenzy, Berserker) only matter on a Gallowdark killzone, which v1 does not have.
- Edition leaks to reject: nothing from earlier-edition Fellgor Ravager cards (no rolled Frenzy tests, no Overwatch, no shape distances, no 2 APL-for-everyone assumptions from 2021), nothing from 40k 10th Chaos or Beastmen rules (no wound rolls, AP, battle-shock, Command phase); inches only, three defence dice, cover save, obscured discards one success, every printed number from the August '26 cards.

### 19.13 As built (M10 batch D)

Built in `src/engine/teams/fellgor-ravagers.ts` (code hooks `fg*`, 14 tests in `tests/engine/teams/fellgor-ravagers.test.ts`, TEAM-FG-000 to 042; scenarios in `fellgor-ravagers.hooks.ts`). Deviations from the Engine map above, each with a RULING in `needs-rules-check.md`:

- Frenzy's damage side is one `onDamageInflicted` handler (War Gong, then Toxic Blessings, then the Frenzy filter). The remaining dice of a Shoot are cut by a per-action effect `fg.frenzyCut` and by zeroing `seq.unblocked`; a fight's dice are all marked used. The end of a counteraction is the `action.ended` hook (the engine has no end-of-counteraction hook), so a counteraction declined with no action leaves a frenzied operative alive.
- Cleaver Flurry is a Fall Back path (`moveKind: 'fallBack'`, `afterMove` hook) with +2" from `moveLimitDelta` while the action is declared, not a team-local path walker; the enemies passed are found by sampling the move's segments every half inch.
- Bloodsense and Apoplectic Rejuvenation read notes written at the damage (`fg.killedInAction`, the `fg.fightKill:<id>` battle ledger) because the kill log is written after the ploy window opens.
- The free offers (Violent Temperament, Gore Marks, Chaos Sigil, Sagacious, Savage) are 0 CP pseudo ploys from the ploy rule (ids `fg.x.*`, `fg.e.*`), never the ploy records, so a free use never touches the strategy ploy. The four flag strategy ploys share the `fgFlagPloy` hook.
- Shared needs (none blocking): operative token looks for `fg.frenzy`, `fg.gongKnell` and `fg.mantle` in `src/client/ui/tokenDefs.ts` (a Frenzy badge); an end-of-counteraction hook; the kill log written before the ploy window of the same step.

## 20. Chaos Cult

Rule IDs `T-CC.<n>`, checklist IDs `TEAM-CC-<nnn>`. Sources: the Chaos Cult team PDF (Kill Team 2024, July '25, including its update log with the July '25 errata and the previous errata; the flow and layout extracts were read together, and the errata page was checked in the PDF itself for colour and strike-through) as the primary source, cross-checked against the Wahapedia Chaos Cult page (faction version 3, June '25), plus the core rules page for terms. Facts read from the PDF are Confirmed; our own calls are Unsourced. The two sources agree on every stat line, weapon and base; they differ only in two places of wording (20.10). All rule text is restated in our own words; team, operative, weapon, ploy and equipment names are used as printed. Core terms per `10-rules-core.md` (R-x.y), missions and universal equipment per `11-missions.md` (M-x.y). Ploys and equipment are one bullet per record so each can carry its MECH line.

Weapon type column: R = ranged, M = melee. Dmg is `normal/crit`. Base is in mm.

### 20.1 Team selection

- T-CC.1 Roster is a fixed list of exactly 14 operatives: 1 CULT DEMAGOGUE (leader), 2 BLESSED BLADE, 9 CHAOS DEVOTEE, 1 ICONARCH, 1 MINDWITCH. There is no choice: every entry is taken, nothing counts as two selections. CHAOS MUTANT and CHAOS TORMENT are never selected; operatives only become them during the battle (T-CC.19 to T-CC.21).
  - MECH: team.json slots `leader` (1, `cc.demagogue`), `blessed-blades` (2, `cc.blessed-blade`, repeatable), `devotees` (9, `cc.devotee`, repeatable), `iconarch` (1), `mindwitch` (1); `cc.mutant` and `cc.torment` are datacard records with `"selectable": false` (in no slot, snapshotted into every game with the team) | CLASS: generic:transformOperative (selectable flag; roster data)
  - RULING: Chaos Cult fixed roster | all 14 operatives are always taken; the builder shows the roster but offers no picks | the selection page lists exact counts with no "up to" and no options | Confirmed
- T-CC.2 Loadouts: every datacard has one fixed loadout (20.3). Demagogue: diabolical stave (ranged and melee profiles) and pistol. Blessed Blade: commune blade. Iconarch: burning censer, pistol, crude melee weapon. Mindwitch: infernal gaze, fists. Devotee: pistol, crude melee weapon. Mutant: blasphemous appendages. Torment: hideous mutations.
  - MECH: datacard `weapons.fixed`, no options | CLASS: data
  - RULING: Chaos Cult Devotee gun name | the Devotee's ranged weapon is the "Pistol" of the datacard, sharing one record with the Demagogue's and the Iconarch's (identical 4 4+ 2/3 Range 8") | the datacard and Wahapedia print "Pistol"; only the selection page's figure caption says "Autopistol" | Confirmed
- T-CC.3 Archetypes: INFILTRATION, SEEK & DESTROY (tac ops out of scope for v1).
  - MECH: team.json `archetypes: ["infiltration", "seek-and-destroy"]` | CLASS: data
- T-CC.4 Keywords and terms: every operative has CHAOS CULT and CHAOS. DARK COMMUNE: Demagogue, Blessed Blades, Iconarch, Mindwitch. PSYKER: Iconarch, Mindwitch. Role keywords DEVOTEE, MUTANT, TORMENT name the three forms. To **MUTATE** is T-CC.20; to **turn into** another operative is T-CC.21. An **ACCURSED GIFT** is one of six rules (T-CC.23 to T-CC.28) a friendly operative has through T-CC.22 or T-CC.34.
  - MECH: keyword lists in operatives.json (DARK COMMUNE with a space, as other teams' two-word keywords) | CLASS: data
